Premkumar, R., Rangaiah, G. P. 2009. Retrofitting conventional column systems to dividing-Wall Columns. Chemical Engineering Research and Design 87(1), 47-60. doi:10.1016/j.cherd.2008.06.013

Locators are printed journal page numbers (PDF page = printed - 46). HYSYS design study (Singapore) of six ternary separations, each designed three ways: conventional two-column system (C2C, mapped distillation-column), new dividing-wall column (DWC, distillation-column_heat-integrated) and the C2C retrofitted to a DWC (R-DWC, technology distillation-column_heat-integrated_retrofit). Main file per application (Tables 4-9 and the Table 10 summary): capacity = feed flow at 100% (Table 11, kg/h), steam specific energy derived from the printed reboiler duty (kW) over the feed (kg/h) x 3.6 = GJ/t of feed, and capex = total module cost (C2C and DWC installed; R-DWC incremental, with the host C2C cost in the same table). Measures: R-DWC reboiler-duty saving (derived), investment and payback per application (Table 10); material-of-construction variants (Table 12); Kolbe and Wenzel 2004 averages (reprinted). Other-values: condenser duties, utility operating cost, steam cost and total annual cost (annualization not stated), Table 11 reduced-capacity retrofits for EWE and alkanes, Table 1 optimization. Not loaded: column sizes and stage counts, bare-module cost breakdown. Traps: no price year printed (CEPCI 560 stated; publication year 2009 used, while UKERC evidently treated the costs as 2007 USD); the denominator is t of FEED separated, not t of a product; Table 9 vs Table 10 alkanes DWC investment 531,729 vs 531,279; depropanizer R-DWC total annual cost (1,119,135) is below its operating cost (printing error). UKERC rows CH-SC1 and CH-BTX1 reconciled in ~/intake/recon.
